reviews.title: Scam bags!
reviews.text:
I downloaded Deepstash after seeing an Instagram advert promoting it as a TikTok style learning app, with engaging AI animations telling stories about history, science and other fascinating subjects.

Unfortunately, the actual experience was nothing like what I expected. Instead, I found what appeared to be primarily an audiobook and reading app, with little resemblance to the animated, visual learning experience shown in the advertising.

I feel the advertising was misleading and that the product did not deliver what persuaded me to download it and start a free trial. I would not recommend it to anyone looking for the kind of engaging, animated educational content shown in its adverts.

I hope Deepstash will make its advertising more representative of the actual experience users can expect.

reviews.title: Money grabbing

I paid more than I usually would for a month and you then doubled that for the following month with no warning. Well you got my money, buyer beware and however good your app is, the arrogance of your actions are apparent and the amounts are obscene. The usual profiteering attitude of success are very apparent. No thanks, however good your app is. Shame on you.

Update: your comment about how much you care was noted and your promise to look into the payment taken was also noted. I have given you a month to look into it and you have not responded. Confidence is lost and, not surprisingly you have not attempted to follow up on your deep concern about my review.

reviews.title: Scam - Don’t Download
reviews.text:
They designed a system much like the Southpark “Terms and Conditions” hyperbole episode. 

They rope you in with a promise of replacing your infinite scrolling with content on books and ideas that increase your knowledge. However what they actually provide is completely useless drivel. 

That drivel is packed into a system they designed to use some third party app to bypass the normal OS subscriptions flows of your phones. When you go to check on useless subscriptions that should be removed, this app doesn’t show up anywhere. What’s more, you likely already deleted this app because you realized right away that it was useless.

Suddenly a year later you are charged $100 (a MASSIVE increase over whatever small price they got you in for), and when you go to the app to cancel and request a refund you are directed towards a website for your operating system to request a refund for subscriptions. The catch, their app doesn’t show up on the list so you can’t even select the app to start the refund process. Then you go to your credit card company, and it becomes a legal battle. 

SCAM through and through.

reviews.title: Same as TikTok?! NOT EVEN CLOSE.
reviews.text:
Same as TikTok?! NOT EVEN CLOSE.
Misleading absolutely!!

I was led to believe this was going to be “like TikTok for thinkers,” meaning it would have the same kind of free, easy, simple, and user-friendly experience. That description is completely misleading.

TikTok is FREE. It is incredibly easy to navigate, easy to connect with, and designed to be user-friendly. Your app cannot honestly be compared to TikTok in that regard.

Yes, I understand that your platform is designed as a learning app. That’s fine. But it isn’t FREE. And when you advertise it as “TikTok for thinkers,” people naturally expect some of the same accessibility and ease of use.

Frankly, I feel like I was misled and had my time wasted because I downloaded this believing I was getting something free and easy to use. If you want people to overlook the other shortcomings of your app, make it FREE first.

The statement “It’s like TikTok for thinkers” is, quite frankly, bull... Don’t compare your product to TikTok when it doesn’t provide the same basic accessibility, simplicity, or mainly FREE user experience.

Thank you for nothing—and thank you for wasting my time.

I accidentally signed up for the trial and realized it the very next day. I emailed their support team within 24 hours to explain the mistake and request a cancellation and refund. They completely refused to process a refund.

The advertising made this app look like a “TikTok for learning”, short engaging content you could scroll through and actually learn something instead of mindlessly scrolling social media. It’s essentially a collection of written summaries and little information cards that you scroll through and read. There’s nothing inherently wrong with that, but it is absolutely not the experience I thought I was purchasing based on the ads.

If I wanted to sit and read condensed articles, I could do that for free. I wanted something visual, quick, engaging, and easy to consume, the educational alternative to TikTok that the advertising made this seem like.

I bought three months and regretted it almost immediately. I’m now requesting a refund. Maybe the app is useful for people specifically looking for written summaries, but if you’re here because the ads made you think you were getting “TikTok, but make it educational,” save your money. reviews.title: FRAUD! SCAM ALERT! FALSE ADVERTISING!
reviews.text: I almost never write these reviews anymore because there are so many fake ones out there that it seems like it is losing its purpose. But I hate these scams so much and I often read one star reviews myself in order to avoid them. So, I'm spending my personal time writing this to tell you that this is one of those apps that claims to have a free version, but instead will trap you in a screen where your only option is to agree to a free trial of the paid version. Theoretically, you could then go back and cancel the free trial and end up with the free version. I will not do that. I recommend boycotting any company that is so manipulative and uses false advertising. It is disgusting and ethically bankrupt. I am exactly the kind of person this app was aimed at--people who are intelligent, educated, and interested in the world rather than social media. I don't understand how the developers could think that intelligent people would not mount a backlash against such a cheap scam. Tell your friends. Boycott. We deserve basic respect as human beings.

reviews.title: Too Expensive for This Economy
reviews.text: You give the option on the app to select that you are downloading Deepstash to “replace social media”. I have never paid $70 a year to have TikTok or any other social media platform — hence why it is an outlet for so many people. In today’s economy where concerts, schooling/classes, movies, etc. are so expensive, especially for those in middle class or lower, people do unfortunately turn to social media for connection, entertainment, content, and to pass time. It is not a true replacement when asking people to go from paying $0 to scroll to $70 to scroll. I understand the content on this app is probably way better to consume on a daily basis than that of other platforms, but I just cannot stand when knowledge or better/healthier options are made inaccessible to the majority of people. Do your thing and keep charging whatever you want, but don’t advertise as a replacement to social media if it’s not feasible one for everyone.

reviews.title: Cannot cancel accidental sub
reviews.text: This may be a brilliant app, but I hate what has become the accepted model where your offered free trial and then if you forget to cancel it, they charge you a large sum and then even if you try to cancel it right away and then you can’t get a live person to explain and ask for a refund. I understand we have personal responsibility, but this happens so much, I think it’s pretty well known by now that it’s an unethical practice. I did the Free trial and meant to check it out, them got sick and it fell through the cracks. As soon as I realized the charge went through, within 24 hours I called and tried to get a hold of someone to cancel and ask for a refund. All I got was AI telling me that no one was available on the phone. I explained that I needed a refund, I don’t have much $ right now and the AI said they said they would let someone know. The fact that I can’t even get ahold of someone to ask for a refund when I haven’t used the app and I made a simple human error and tried to resolve it as soon as possible is a representation of one of the biggest problems in the world today… Lack of humanity.

reviews.title: Rich
reviews.text: Just downloaded and started to try deep stash and after the first item I am forced to watch an advert for “paladin” in its own description an addictive scrolling app…. Right, so you got me to try your app to aviod doom scrolling then within minutes you have me watching adverts for addictive scrolling time bandit apps?  Task Switch Deleted - Eat your own dog food you lost me…

reviews.title: Superficial, boring and empty
reviews.text: Apologies to the makers of this app as it’s clear some work has gone into it, but it’s very bad. This app boils ideas down to nothing but these incredibly simplistic and superficial stories that, ironically, are all padding. I found myself skipping through the stories - which the app reads aloud infuriatingly - as they are all the same and very dull. Then you get to the ideas at the end, and they always incredibly basic, for example: “the more stuff you own, the more stuff owns you”. Great. I didn’t need a boring story to get to that point and it doesn’t help me remember. Instead I’m thinking, why does that happen? And what’s the evidence for this? But the ideas aren’t explored, explained or evidenced, they are just asserted. Also, there’s nothing surprising or interesting about the ideas, there’s no nuance. The app just asserts some very boring and basic ideas in a very drawn out way - the opposite of what it intends. There’s definitely a market for an app like this, that introduces you new and interesting ideas and explains what the evidence says - but this isn’t it.

reviews.title: Misleading
reviews.text:
Deepstash positions itself as doom scrolling for intellectuals. The irony is it’s the same exact thing it criticizes wearing a fancier hat. Slow down and apply critical thinking. Back in school those who read the cliff notes rather than reading the book were often considered lazy. They didn’t care about understanding the book they wanted to spout off just enough to make it seem like they understand as much as someone who did read it. Thats who you want to be? Ew lol. 

Tik Tok is entertainment. Comparing it to education is some apples to orange nonsense. Either Harvard doesn’t understand this, or, understands calling you a moron for using social media will siphon a number of people to put ad spend and subscription revenue in their pockets instead. Looks like they accomplished this wonderfully. 

This app is the social media equivalent of people whose self growth journey begins and ends at buying self help books. Always consuming never applying. Feeling accomplished because they read another fact about self empowerment. 

If that’s who you want to be I have bad news for you, this app isn’t for intellectuals it’s for procrastinators. If you genuinely want to learn more, know more, and do more, the only substitute is putting in your 10,000 hours to do so. 

Just really take a moment to think. “Morons doom scroll on social media, you arent stupid are you? I didn’t think so. Good boy. Good dopamine monkey. Scroll here.” 

Absolutely ridiculous this is merely a shinning example of

reviews.title: Should be a -5
reviews.text:
I wish I could recommend this app, but my experience has been extremely disappointing. The biggest issue is the lack of customer service. When problems are brought to their attention, they simply do not respond. They do not communicate, resolve issues, or seem interested in listening to their customers.

An app is only as good as the support behind it, and unfortunately that has not been my experience. I hope the developers improve their communication and begin taking customer concerns seriously. The app has real potential, but without responsive customer support, I cannot recommend it.

This version is more concise, reads more naturally, and focuses on your experience rather than making broader claims that could be challenged.

reviews.title: Childish and Misleadingly Promoted
reviews.text:
It was pretty much a rule of thumb for me to never buy anything I saw promoted in a social media feed. Subscribing to Deepstash has only served to strengthen that view. 

It's being pushed as a TikTok alternative providing intellectual stimulation instead of shallow, empty gratification, so I was expecting it to serve up a bunch of random stuff from quality sources aligned to my stated interests: gourmet tapas for a hungry brain. But that's not it. It's more like a self-help app for mouth breathers, with the same kind of vibe as a basic language learning course. I'm writing this review after a mere 15 minutes of trying the app, and I'm already feeling that my IQ has dropped a couple of notches.

The little flame thing that keeps popping up to tell me how well I'm doing is unpleasantly reminiscent of Clippy, the widely loathed MS Office assistant. I hate it already, and it seems deeply unlikely that I will ever consider my three-month subscription to be money well spent. I just feel stupid for my lack of due diligence. Try before you buy.

reviews.title: Not worth the amounts they want
reviews.text:
The “learning” is shallow and repetitive. The illustrations are real minimum-effort — female-name characters illustrated with a male character, cheesy interpretations of similes from the text etc. 
The “practice” multi-choices are truly trivial and do nothing to reinforce learning - and sometimes even seem to contradict what you’ve just read. 
The app started beeping and pinging at me even with the phone in Silent mode, which is pretty disgracefully lazy on the part of the their testers. 
The subscription amount is way in excess of the value you could possibly get from this. 
Don’t waste your money! Don’t waste your time “reading” a book this way!

reviews.title: MISLEADING and STUPID
reviews.text: So disappointed. I should have read the reviews first. Complete bait and switch! It's advertised as an alternative to social media doom scrolling, as if it would let you scroll and it would present cool ideas, smart quotes, intelligent or intriguing concepts, videos, memes, etc. And by comparison to social media, it implies that its algorithms would present ideas based on your interests. No. What it does instead is show you a list of books to read. That's it. Books. Not quotes. Not cool ideas. No videos or memes. You don't scroll between them like social media. It just shows you book titles, you click on one, and it summarizes the main point of each chapter as you swipe left.  AND it's presented in a childish way like we're too dumb to understand the actual book. Like "thought-leading books for dummies" instead of "Smarter scrolling for intellectual types."  It doesn't use algorithms- it makes you take a quiz that already pigeon-holes what it will show you. And it gamifies the reading like Duolingo.  Honestly the whole thing is insulting. I can't believe I paid $11 for a min and SO glad I didn't sign up for more. It's such a scam. It would never ever compare to, let alone replace, social media scrolling. I want my money back!

reviews.title: Mediocre value, annual subscription lock in
reviews.text: The advertisement promised, with breathtaking prose, that with Deepstash I would shift my social media habits into a learning experience every day with deep stash. Unfortunately, the material that was available was surface level, possibly AI-written summaries of books that others have written about in greater detail and with more relevance to everyday work and life. It’s fine if this isn’t the perfect app for me, maybe it does work for someone. Unfortunately, I just missed the cancellation window and so now I’ve paid $70 for a year of this service … there seems to be no way to reverse the charge or do anything to change it. There’s no monthly billing, only annual billing. So if you sign up for the “free one week trial” you’d better be careful you know precisely when your time runs out. Otherwise you’ll be out $70.

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text:
I had cancelled my subscription and deleted my account several days before my renewal date, yet I was still charged for an additional 3 months. When I contacted customer support, they were not helpful in resolving the issue and  didn’t provide a satisfactory explanation for why the charges went through. 

The experience has been frustrating and disappointing. Customers should be able to trust that cancelling a subscription and  deleting an account before renewal will prevent future charges. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this app.

reviews.title: Repetitive
reviews.text: I found it way too boring for my tastes. After scrolling through countless books, I found each repeating the same ideas over and over again. The app prides itself on getting you to learn new things and get rid of doomscrolling. The issue is, it’s not nearly as fun as they make it sound. You learn one thing over and over again and if you already knew it: tough luck. I also found the breadth of categories lacklustre. There was nothing on LGBTQ+ for example, something I’m really passionate about. The history categories were just the main big ideas, no niche topics. As someone who considers themself well read, this was disheartening and frustrating. It’s fine for children being introduced to these ideas but for adults, whom the app does market towards, it just doesn’t have enough to offer.

reviews.title: Beware fraud and Deceptive terms and sign up practices
reviews.text: Company commits fraud.  They charged my credit card without providing the notice they state they give.  I reported to my credit card company.  They lied the the cc company so dispute was not covered and they have reduced my subscription to the free one so they effectively stole my money and did not provide a product.  I will now be filing a complaint with the BBB and State Attorney General’s Office since they have committed wire fraud.  Beware of their deceptive billing practices.  When signing up it said it would give a reminder notice of free period ending.  It did not.  It also redirects you to their website during sign up so they do not have to follow apples terms.  I tried to follow their directions to cancel and get a refund from apple only to find out Apple does not show the purchase only to download of the app.  The purchase looks to have take place on their website and they don’t have a way to get a refund through the website or it is very well hidden.  It’s not a bad product, just sketchy business practices.

reviews.title: £70 Charge after Free Trial
reviews.text: Signed up for the 7-day free trial and got no reminder whatsoever that it was ending, then suddenly I’m charged £70 for a full year. There was nothing clear at sign-up to say it would roll straight into an annual subscription. That feels really misleading. To be honest, the app itself was underwhelming anyway, but the way the payment is handled is what’s left the worst impression. Very disappointing.

reviews.title: Can’t even start the trial
reviews.text: I downloaded the app, put in my email and chose the subjects I was interested in.  It then progressed to starting the free 7 day trial, when I click on that button it takes me back to the App Store.  When I try to communicate with the developer it takes me to a website where it again asks me for my interests, there is no link on the website to contact the developer.  This app is not ready for distribution and goes against European GDPR regulations for clear communication as there is no mechanism for me to tell the developer to delete my information if I wanted to.

reviews.title: They trap you for ongoing service
reviews.text: Last month I was unexpectedly charged $50 for a premium service from this company that I did not want. I set up a trial. I barely used it. I completely forgot about it and as soon as the charge came through, I immediately disputed it before it even posted to my account. I reached out to the company and they basically told me that they are not obligated to refund me and it’s in their terms of service. I reminded them that I don’t use their service. I didn’t use it and they had just charged me and I wanted my money back because what they are doing is stealing from me. They told me to pound sand and in a condescending manner offered me a partial refund of $25 which they reminded me they weren’t obligated to do. Like they are doing me a favor by giving half of my money that they were stealing back. They forced me to open a merchant dispute, which of course I won. There are laws in California that regulate automatic renewal license licenses called ARL’s. They are in violation of these rules. I don’t recommend this app and the customer service is atrocious.

reviews.title: Payment.
reviews.text: I am not paying money to scroll a replacement for social media. If the aim was to get people off of social media, then you wouldn’t discourage that by charging a subscription plan at the same price as streaming services. I understand these things cost money to make but that’s why ads exist. I was fully invested in trying this platform out and ready to replace social media. But there is no chance I’m paying to do that.

reviews.title: Pointless and unresponsive
reviews.text: It really doesn't work. You have to have the phone on and screen on to listen to the ebook summary. The summary is not great and also, the subscription was triggered despite my cancellation and no amount of writing g to them made a bit of difference, as they just don't respond. Go buy a book and read it. Much better all round. Don't bother.

reviews.title: I love the idea of this app, but...
reviews.text: So to start off, the idea of this app is amazing, and I love the UI. It's easy to use, you learn new things every day, and it helps keep me away from social media or mindless games when I'm bored. However, the rampant use of AI in the app is beyond annoying. The art slides don't make sense. A story will show slides of the main character being completely different in each slide. Different race, different facial features, even different genders. On top of that, I've found multiple grammatical and spelling errors within the stories, which tells me there's not even a human editor. And for the app subscription to be so expensive when they have so few actual people working on it makes no sense. $40 for a year or $200 for a lifetime (and mind you this is with their special offers, not regular price) is horrendous. If it had real art, writers, and editors, I might consider paying that but spending that much to support AI is just sad. I'll stick with the free version.

reviews.title: Hard to cancel
reviews.text: Signed up for a 7 day trial period. At the end of the sign up process, a small icon  for a discounted rate appears. Icon was not accompanied by any explanation that it nulls a trial period and that the discount rate is essentially a purchase of an annual subscription. I only found out when credit card was charged as soon as I submitted. Reached out to DS and explained I would rather have paid the full price with a trial period so I have an option to cancel after exploring the app. The response was no. I filed a dispute with my credit card company. The credit card company provided me with a response from Deepstash, and they provided “evidence” of an email that I sent asking them to cancel my subscription even though my 7 day trial period ended. Not the most trustworthy so watch out.

reviews.title: Do yourself a favour and skip it.
reviews.text:
- Content is incredibly weak and samey
- Price is ludicrously high once the trial ends
- Just read an effing book every now and again for heavens sake! It’s cheaper, far more rewarding and infinitely more enriching. 
- I have nothing whatsoever positive to say about my experience on something that just seems to be an attempt to cash in on people’s shortening attention spans. There is nothing of value being offered here that can’t be found elsewhere in a far more nourishing form. (And pretty much guaranteed cheaper)

reviews.title: Do not get this app.
reviews.text: Did the free trial, did not like the app. Was supposed to get an email letting me know that the free trial was up and never got it. I realize it’s my fault for not cancelling the free trial on time, but when a company says “you’ll get an email 2 days before” I didn’t set the usual reminder. I emailed support after I was charged $70 for an app that I have barely used, and was told there was nothing they could do. You’d think for an app that is advertised to help adhd and mental health they would be more mindful when people email asking for help when they get charged for the pro. Instead this app is just capitalizing on forgetful adhd people and getting their $70 and then being rude and refusing to offer money back because it’s out of their control. The app did not help reduce my doom scrolling and has so many other problems in addition to their customer support being awful.

reviews.title: Robbery
reviews.text: Wanted to try it out during the free subscription forgot about it and got charged $70 for a year subscription. I went in to try and cancel and prevent payment since it said took affect the next day and was unable to do so. I canceled my membership to make sure I wouldn’t get charged for anything again anyway and received an email about getting 67% off after I said I was leaving because it was expensive and I didn’t like getting charged $70 for a full year right away. So I used that and it charged me for another year. After reaching out to support to refund one of these charges, I was told I didn’t use the app enough and have to have used it for at least five days but they’ll give me 24 months extra use. Ridiculous business strategy don’t trust them!!

reviews.title: AVOID AT ALL COST
reviews.text:
TERRIBLE customer service and a complete waste of money.

It takes them nearly 14 days just to respond to my support request, and when they finally did it was nothing more than an automated message that clearly hadn’t addressed my issue at all. There seems to be a total lack of care for customers once they’ve taken your money.

The app itself is also very poor. It doesn’t offer much value and definitely isn’t worth the price they charge. Between the slow responses, automated replies, and overall lack of support, the experience has been incredibly frustrating.

I would NOT recommend this app to anyone !!!!!!

reviews.title: AI
reviews.text: I really don’t like the AI summaries of books that it’s peddling on the main page. The summaries are all the same structure and use the same story format. Sometimes they’ve not scanned the AI summary or AI generated images so it’s just garbled nonsense. It’s just a bit lazy really and I prefer reading the human generated summaries of books. Make your users’ summaries the main feature - the AI stories should be available but not front and centre.

reviews.title: Used to love it, but the recent changes ruined what made it special
reviews.text:
I originally downloaded Deepstash because it was a refreshing mix of quick quotes, standalone ideas, short insights from articles, books, podcasts, and more. It felt like a real alternative to mindless scrolling—bite-sized wisdom you could browse freely by topic or search for specific concepts without committing to a full summary.
But they’ve completely shifted the app. They got rid of most of the standalone quotes and loose ideas, and now everything is locked behind full book summaries (or at least what they call “ideas” that are just excerpts tied to books). When I search for a topic or idea I used to find easily, half the results are missing, or I have to click into a longer book summary to even see anything relevant. You can’t just casually read and collect random powerful ideas anymore; it’s all funneled into these structured book breakdowns.
I loved the diversity before—different books, articles, videos, user-contributed stuff, motivational quotes, practical tips from various sources. Now it feels way more homogenized and limited. The material lacks diversity too; it’s heavy on the usual self-help/business/pop-psychology suspects with not much variety or depth in other areas.
Success seems to have turned Deepstash into just another generic book summary app—exactly like the ones it used to stand out from. Good while it lasted, but the magic is gone. I’m deleting it and moving on. Disappointed.

reviews.title: Fraud
reviews.text:
This app is a scam. I downloaded with high hopes and wasn’t impressed with the content. I deleted the app and checked iTunes to verify there wasn’t an upcoming purchase for the yearly subscription. No subscription or upcoming subscription payments were shown through iTunes. 

BUT, this scam of an app still managed to charge my card NOT THROUGH ITUNES and refuses to refund my payment. I have tried speaking with Deepstash and they won’t answer any of my questions directly. They did admit they didn’t charge me through iTunes (not sure how they can do that if the app was downloaded through iTunes). The only resolution they offered was an additional 2 years subscription for “free”. Why would I want longer access to an app that has already scammed me with their greedy fine print and questionable billing methods?

reviews.title: Used to be awesome…
reviews.text:
I’ve used DeepStash for a couple of years now and have always really enjoyed it. Several months ago, after more than a year of having a paid subscription, I had to cancel my subscription due to a change in my financial situation. Up until the latest update the app was still very usable even without the paid version.

After the most recent changes, though, the experience has become frustrating enough that the app is almost useless to me.

The quick read feature is completely different now. It no longer shows suggested single ideas/cards on the home page the way it used to, and you can’t move through consecutive ideas without watching ads. That alone would be tolerable if the ads worked properly, but they often don’t. I just had to sit through three separate 30-second ads before the app finally advanced. If you try to close the ad, it forces you to start another one, and you end up stuck in a loop wondering whether the ad will actually register or not.

I understand developers need to make money, and subscriptions are part of that. But the new design feels less like encouragement to subscribe and more like the free version has been intentionally crippled. Removing the single-idea suggestions from the home screen was disappointing enough, but the current ad system makes the whole experience clunky and frustrating.

DeepStash used to be a genuinely great app. I hope the team reconsiders some of these changes because the current version really undermines what made it so good in th

reviews.title: Scam
reviews.text: Took £50 out of my account after I deleted my account and the app. Re downloaded it to see and I’d been signed up to a subscription even though I had cancelled it. Reported it to my bank and the company disputed it even though I did not use the service! Don’t download - it’s not even full writings, it’s people’s short interpretations of books :(

reviews.title: Rubbish AI generated content + scammy billing practises
reviews.text:
Firstly, if you want to learn the key points of a well regarded book you would be better off just asking Chat GPT to give you this, than you would be using this app. 
Secondly, they make it very difficult to unsubscribe (and you need to unsubscribe because you have to enter your card details, even for a free trial). To unsubscribe you must login to their website. There is no unsubscribe option in the app or the App Store.

reviews.title: Scam!!  Avoid at all costs
reviews.text: This company is terrible to deal with. I cancelled my free trial but they still charged me the following month. They are doing everything in their power to avoid refunding me for a 2 days of a month I didn’t use. They have no ethics and are part of the subscription trap scam the government needs to crack down on. Currently fighting with my bank about this and reporting them to trading standards. Stolen £50 from me, daylight robbery!

reviews.title: Charged Even After I Canceled
reviews.text: I’m really unhappy with this company. I canceled my subscription last year immediately after the promotion price I received for the initial 3 months. The cancelation process is convoluted and confusing to start but when I looked in the app, it said Valid Until (Date) so it seemed like it had canceled correctly. But I just got charged for another 3 months at the full $50 price. So I went and canceled AGAIN. And again, the app now says Valid Until (date). It smells a little scammy. I get that Apple takes a cut if they use the standard in-app payment system, but it protects consumers from shady cancelation loops like this. Now I get to set a reminder to see if they try to charge me again, even though I’ve canceled twice now. I wouldn’t do business with this company again.

reviews.title: Wanna feel ripped off?? Subscribe to this app
reviews.text: This app or platform is NOT worth a yearly subscription, or any cost above free. What you get for the amount you pay isn’t value added at all; it feels like I’m being ripped off by greedy developers looking to make a buck off folks who are tired of traditional social media. As much as I love learning new things and continuous self improvement, this ain’t it. The “bite-sized” micro learning elements are so bite sized you’re left starving. That’s not micro learning, it’s lowkey rage baiting. It keeps tally of my “ideas” read, when all I’m doing is reading random quotes loosely based off the particular wormhole I choose to crawl down that day. After about 5min, I’m bored, and haven’t actually LEARNED anything other than slowly coming to the realization I HATE THIS APP, AND I WAS STUPID ENOUGH TO PAY MONEY FOR IT. Once the developers actually make a product worth a yearly subscription, maybe I’d reconsider…but probably not. At this point, I could gain more motivation and micro learning from one of those desktop calendars with cloyingly syrupy motivational quotes on them that your Aunt Betty had in a dusty corner of her house from 1997.

reviews.title: Take off the unneccesary stuff
reviews.text: This isn’t a game and I’m now a child. The achievements are meaningless and useless. I don’t want to share what I’ve earned either. It is useless in the realm of learning in an app. Please remove it. Also please allow a selection for the voice when reading. Needs to add background music option as well. This is designed as if it’s a game for children. This is a paid  app and the design, development, and execution should be on par, esp with an annual subscription. Get rid of streaks and all the other nonsense that stops me from being able to read and listen to the information. Also need to actually curate the information put together. I listened to something about emotional intelligence and the very next topic was that emotional intelligence is overrated. Seriously…need to put more thought into a paid app. All this fluff is no value add and basically the same as ads.

reviews.title: Scam - avoid at all cost!
reviews.text: The app was advertised to me on Instagram and I thought I will give it a go. Long story short, the app was really not engaging and defeat the purpose of trying to divert my doomscrolling to something better. I emailed them to request a refund and they first said I wasn’t eligible because I haven’t used enough, then when I did, they offered to give me a lifetime subscription. When I said I don’t want that and want a refund instead, I don’t hear back from them despite multiple chasers, which confirmed to me that they’re a scam. Avoid if you can!

reviews.title: Scam
reviews.text: After screens with ‘7 day trial period’ there was suddenly a cut price subscription on the checkout screen that wasn’t mentioned previously. They sneakily do NOT mention that this tier has no trial period, meaning payment was immediate. I alerted them to this immediately and made a claim via the App Store for a refund- I haven’t used the app at all and I’ve been refunded for a basic misunderstanding like this in the past. Not this time. Scam. £40 stolen.

reviews.title: Slow and clunky
reviews.text:
Ok, this is early days so this is a review from someone still
Learning.  I find the platform very slow to load many times 15-20 seconds or more. A bit annoying in this day snd age. You dont know if you've hit a null search or what. Problematic for a platform that is supposed to be quick. Second it is hard to navigate and find things. Bookmark something. Where does it go? Oh to "library " not to a tab marker bookmarks or even your library vs the library. Want to store a quote? You don't share it but bookmark it again. Of course over time you can figure these things out but been surprised how clunky the whole platform is. Disappointed

reviews.title: Don’t even download this app
reviews.text:
A “7-day free trial” is advertised when you’re shown the yearly plan, but if you choose the monthly option, the trial quietly disappears. This isn’t made clear upfront, and it’s easy to assume the trial applies regardless of plan — which feels intentionally misleading.

When I contacted support, I was told they couldn’t issue a refund and that only Apple could, which hasn’t been true in my past experiences with other apps. Deflecting responsibility instead of helping the customer further eroded my trust. Response times were also extremely slow (about 5 days per reply).

The product itself doesn’t justify a paid “education” label. I noticed multiple typos within minutes, and the content felt shallow and unoriginal — more like copy-pasted material than actual instruction. Not worth paying for.
